# Kestrel (02, engineer) — BAD-053

## Brief
The boundary test you are fixing is `test/server/admin-actions-boundary.test.mjs`, added by PR 1 of BAD-053 ([0snug0/BadTakes#370](https://github.com/0snug0/BadTakes/pull/370), commit `1186233`). It passes on macOS and Linux and fails on Windows. Every other check on the PR is green; this is the only thing holding the merge.

## The failure

`test-windows` reports one failure out of 1403:

```
not ok 965 - the support leaves under lib/actions/ carry no directive
  error: "lib\\actions\\auth-admin.ts must open with import 'server-only'; — it holds code that must never reach the browser"
```

## The diagnosis, already made — confirm it before you act on it

Around line 183 the assertion reads the first line with `src.split('\n')[0]` and compares it strict-equal against `"import 'server-only';"`. The Windows runner checks out with CRLF line endings, so the first element is `"import 'server-only';\r"` and the equality fails. The file on disk is correct; the assertion is what is wrong.

The two neighbouring checks already tolerate it and are the pattern to follow:

- `directiveLineIn` (line 60) matches `/^\s*(['"])use server\1\s*;?\s*$/` per line — `\r` is whitespace, so `\s*$` absorbs it.
- The barrel's leftovers check (around line 259) maps `line.trim()` over the split before filtering.

That is why assertion (b) is the only one that failed while (a), (c) and (d) passed.

## What to do

Make every line-based assertion in this file line-ending agnostic, not just the one that failed. Read the whole file and audit each place it splits on `\n` or compares a line, then fix them as a set. The Windows runner found one; leaving a sibling brittle only defers the same red check to PR 2, which adds five more files for these assertions to walk.

Two constraints on how you fix it:

- **Do not weaken what is asserted.** The support leaves must still be required to *open* with `import 'server-only';` on their first line — not merely contain it somewhere, and not merely start with something matching loosely. A CRLF-tolerant check of the same strictness is the goal; an assertion that would now pass on a file whose first line is a comment is a regression, and worse than the failure it replaces, because this is the file that stands between `deleteAuthUser` and a public endpoint.
- **Only this file changes.** Do not add a `.gitattributes` entry, do not normalise line endings in the repository, and do not touch `admin/src/lib/actions/`. The source files are fine; a checkout is allowed to have CRLF.

If while auditing you find an assertion that is brittle for some reason other than line endings, fix it if it is the same kind of defect, and `proposal file` it if it is not.

## Verify

From the repo root:

```
node --test test/server/admin-actions-boundary.test.mjs
```

Then prove the fix actually addresses CRLF rather than passing by accident on your LF checkout: write a CRLF copy of the two support leaves into a scratch directory outside the repository and run the same assertions against it, or otherwise demonstrate the check holds for both line endings. Quote what you ran and what it printed. A green run on a machine that never produced the failing condition proves nothing, and saying so is better than claiming a fix you could not exercise.

Also re-run the neighbours so the set still passes together:

```
node --test test/server/admin-moderation.test.mjs test/server/admin-pool.test.mjs test/server/admin-client-boundary.test.mjs test/server/admin-actions-boundary.test.mjs
```

## Done when

Every line-based assertion in the file holds under both LF and CRLF with its strictness intact, you have exercised the CRLF case rather than assumed it, all four test files pass together, and the change is left uncommitted in the worktree for Spud to commit onto the open PR.
